stem: A heart recipient's caregiver calls reporting sudden facial drooping, arm weakness, and slurred speech. Which instruction aligns with standard urgent-contact education?

options.text: Contact the transplant team promptly because stroke symptoms are urgent matters
Schedule this concern for discussion at the next routine medication refill call
Wait 72 hours to see if symptoms resolve before any outreach
Stop all immunosuppression at home without notifying the team

explanation.rationale_correct: Signs of stroke using FAST recognition (facial weakness, arm weakness, speech problems, time to act) are listed as urgent reasons to contact the transplant team.

rationale_incorrect.B: Stroke symptoms are urgent matters, not non-urgent refill or scheduling calls.
rationale_incorrect.C: Acute neurologic symptoms require prompt evaluation without multi-day delay.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppression changes require coordinated team management during acute neurologic evaluation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → §h. Communication with the transplant team → iii. Urgent matters (FAST stroke)
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Signs of stroke: FAST … Facial weakness Arm weakness Speech problems Time to act

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → §h. Communication → iii. Urgent matters (FAST stroke symptoms); PDF p. 111 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

stem: A kidney recipient on tacrolimus develops rising serum creatinine and hypertension. Which adverse effect profile is MOST consistent with this medication class?

options.text: Permanent cure of pre-transplant diabetes without monitoring
Graft tenderness as the hallmark of calcineurin inhibitor toxicity
No effect on blood pressure or renal function

explanation.rationale_correct: Tacrolimus is a calcineurin inhibitor associated with nephrotoxicity, hypertension, hyperglycemia, and other adverse effects requiring therapeutic monitoring.

rationale_incorrect.B: Tacrolimus may cause hyperglycemia; it does not permanently cure diabetes.
rationale_incorrect.C: Calcineurin inhibitor toxicity does not produce graft tenderness; rising creatinine and hypertension are more characteristic.
rationale_incorrect.D: CNIs commonly affect renal function and blood pressure.

stem: When a candidate is listed in the UNOS candidate database (UNet), which candidate information is entered as part of standard waitlist registration data?

options.text: Blood type, height, weight, and other clinical variables
Only the candidate's personal social media identifiers
Only the surgeon's operative note from a prior unrelated surgery

explanation.rationale_correct: Waitlist registration in UNet includes candidate blood type, height, weight, and other clinical variables used for allocation matching.

rationale_incorrect.B: UNet registration uses clinical and demographic listing variables, not social media identifiers.
rationale_incorrect.C: Discharge medication schedules are post-transplant care documents, not primary UNet listing fields.
rationale_incorrect.D: Prior unrelated operative notes are not the described UNet candidate registration data set.

stem: A coordinator is teaching staff about late post-transplant mortality and long-term complication surveillance. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Cardiovascular disease is among the leading causes of death in the late post-transplantation period.
Cancer is among the leading causes of death in the late post-transplantation period.
Infection plays no role in late post-transplant mortality.
Immunosuppression contributes to the pathogenesis of late cardiovascular, cancer, and infectious complications.

explanation.rationale_correct: Late post-transplant mortality is driven substantially by cardiovascular disease, cancer, and infection, with immunosuppression contributing to each. Statement III is false because infection remains a leading late cause of death.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—immunosuppression contributes to late CVD, cancer, and infection.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement III is false; infection is a leading late mortality cause.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false; not all four statements are correct.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 11, Post-transplant Long-term Management → late mortality paragraph (CVD, cancer, infection)
primary_anchor.quote_hint: CVD, cancer, and infection are the leading causes of death in the late post-transplantation period, and immunosuppression plays a major role

references.locator: Ch. 11 → late post-transplant mortality (statements I, II, IV; negation of III); PDF p. 302 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).
